newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria, France agree to boost economic ties.
newsitem.headline: Syria, France agree to boost economic ties.

text.p: Syria and France agreed on Sunday to boost economic cooperation after solving the 1.8 francs ($350 million) of Syrian debt to Paris that hindered trade ties for over a decade.

Head of the Syrian chamber of commerce Rateb Shallah said both sides have agreed to revive the supreme Syrian-French cooperation committee and to put a deal to avoid double taxation between the two countries.

Shallah told Reuters after a meeting with French officials over improving trade ties between Damascus and Paris that the committee will include six members of each side from both private and government sectors.
The committee will study improving the fields of cooperation and work to find new fields.
French commercial consultant in Damascus Jean-Louis Fontenille said France was looking to be the major partner for Syria.
He said a "bright" future of relations and cooperation between Syria and France will start after the current visit of French President Jacques Chirac to Damascus.

France is seeking to enter the Syrian market and investment sectors, specially electricity, irrigation, transport and banking sectors. Paris also wants to increase its equipment and machinery exports to Syria, Fontenille said.

France, which is handling the project of modernising the operations of the central bank of Syria, is seeking to participate in the irrigation projects on the Khabour and Tigris rivers in the northeast.
"Syria is a good place for investment. There are raw materials, experience and enough labour," the French commercial consultant said.
The French petroluem company Elf has invested around $600 million over the last six years in exploration and exploitation operations in Syria, he said.
"Both parties want to enhance cooperation and France is seeking to be the major partner for Syria. France is now the second client and fifth supplier for Syria," he said.
Syria's exports to France in 1995, according to official statistics, were 6.4 billion Syrian pounds. Syria's imports from France were 1.8 billion pounds.
The statistic's calculations were made at the exchange rate of 11.2 pounds per U.S. dollar. The black market rate is 50 pounds for a dollar.
Syria exports mainly oil, raw materials and textiles to France and imports equipment and machinery.
